Version gating in code: writers use `formatVersion` to decide manifest behavior (e.g. SnapshotProducer.java:147, 155 branches on format version). The spec's Appendix E v2 list is what makes position/equality deletes appear together (v2 lines 39-45), and v3/v4 add DV and drop writes as above.

## Compaction (rewrite)

Compaction rewrites a set of data files so the rows are re-serialized into new files — which is exactly the mechanism that *materializes* deletes. `RewriteFiles` is the operation: it says "replace these data/delete files, add these new ones" (BaseRewriteFiles.java:48-116). The action planning (BaseRewriteDataFilesAction) reads the old files, applies the applicable deletes to drop deleted rows, and writes new files with only the survivors.

Two things matter:

1. What compaction does to deletes: when it rewrites a data file, the deletes that covered it are folded into the new data — the deleted rows simply aren't written. Old data files and now-superseded delete files are removed from the snapshot. This is the exact semantics of `deleteFile(...)`/`addFile(...)` on `RewriteFiles` (BaseRewriteFiles.java:48-68). The spec calls compaction a `replace` operation and notes "Data and delete files were added and removed without changing table data" (Snapshot operation enum, spec line 974; code `operation()` for rewrites returns REPLACE).

2. The safety rule: a rewrite must never accidentally re-introduce or drop deletes. So `RewriteFiles.validate` enforces `validateNoNewDeletesForDataFiles` — if you're replacing a data file, there must be **no new row-level deletes targeting it** that appeared after the rewrite was planned; otherwise the commit is rejected (BaseRewriteFiles.java:135-142, validate at line 140). This is why the rewrite is based on a specific `startingSnapshotId` and must be re-applied against the same lineage.

Separately, Iceberg ships a **delete-file compaction** action that rewrites/lays-out position-delete entries (and, in v3, merges position deletes into DVs) — see `RewritePositionDeletesCommitManager` and `BinPackRewritePositionDeletePlanner` (actions package). The spec mandates v3 writers merge position deletes into DVs when maintaining them (spec line 1366, Appendix E v3 line 1950-1956), so delete compaction in v3 converges old position-delete files into DVs.
